title: Inter-variant tokenizer & tooling parity checklist and CI gates
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Maintain and extend a lightweight, executable compatibility checklist that verifies tokenizer behavior, context window mapping, and public tooling (tool-calling signatures, structured output hooks) across fallback model variants used by smart routing policies. Goal is to reduce runtime surprises when routing to a fallback variant by catching tokenizer/context and tooling regressions before deploys.

Scope:
- Positive tests for tokenizer tokenization equivalence on canonical prompts and edge cases (Unicode, emojis, long prefix preservation).
- Context window sanity mapping: ensure truncated/truncation-position semantics are documented and tested across variants.
- Tooling parity checks: function/tool calling signatures, JSON schema conformance, and streaming token boundaries.
- CI gate integration: quick runnable checks that run as part of model onboarding and variant rollout pipelines.

Out of scope: full model fidelity comparisons (quality/regression evals), large-scale synthetic token-level diffing across entire corpora (can be follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:
- A canonical checklist document lives in Confluence and is referenced by the variant rollout playbook.
- A runnable test harness (<= 200s runtime) that validates tokenizer parity + one tooling smoke test per variant is added to the model onboarding pipeline.
- Any mismatches produce deterministic failure messages and suggested remediation steps.
- Owners assigned for failing variants and a clear rollback/override policy for emergency routing continues to exist in the Console rollout UI.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist published and linked from variant rollout playbook
Test harness added to onboarding CI and green on baseline variants
Deterministic failure messages with remediation guidance
Owner and rollback policy documented and wired to Console rollout metadata
tasks: Draft canonical tokenizer edge-case list (Unicode, combining chars, surrogate pairs, long-prefix preservation)
Implement fast tokenizer parity runner (Python) that compares token ids and normalized text roundtrip
Add context-window mapping tests for truncation offsets and prefix-preserve flags
Add one tooling smoke test: function-calling signature validation + schema roundtrip
Integrate runner into model onboarding CI (GitHub Actions) with a ~3-minute timeout
Document failure modes and remediation steps in playbook and Console rollout help text
risks: False positives due to minor tokenizer byte-level differences that do not affect downstream generation
CI flakiness if runtime environment mismatches tokenizer C-extension builds
Additional onboarding time for some experimental model variants increases time-to-prod
mitigations: Whitelist acceptable diff classes and normalize on Unicode NFC before comparison
Containerize the runner with pinned tokenizer binaries to reduce environment skew
Provide an expedited override path in Console for emergency routing with explicit risk acknowledgement
